Consult Summary:
- 50-year-old man with 4–5 days of cough, runny nose, sore throat, subjective fevers/sweats, myalgias, and reported shortness of breath; clinical impression of viral illness/early influenza; supportive care advised with a delayed amoxicillin prescription if no improvement in 24–48 hours; follow-up if not better by next week.

History:
- Presenting complaint: “Run-down” with cough and cold symptoms.
- Timeline:
  - Onset: Saturday (≈4–5 days prior to consult).
  - Course: Persistent since onset; initial mild diarrhea resolved.
- Cough:
  - Mostly dry; worse in the morning.
  - Admits a small amount of phlegm.
- Upper respiratory symptoms:
  - Runny nose.
  - Sore throat (notes recent shouting at football matches).
  - No significant ear pain; hearing “not as good as it used to be,” but overall “all right.”
- Breathing:
  - Conflict noted: initially implies not more breathless, later states breathing “not good” and confirms feeling more short of breath.
  - Denies chest pain.
- Systemic:
  - Subjective fever/chills/sweats (nighttime blankets on/off). No thermometer used.
  - Myalgias/joint stiffness (generalized, worse with bending and movement).
- Gastrointestinal:
  - Day 1: mild diarrhea, now resolved.
  - Denies nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain.
- Appetite/hydration: Appetite okay; keeping up with fluids.
- Exposures/triggers: None identified; symptoms started after dining out (no suspected foodborne cause).

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- History of high blood pressure (previously told BP was high; currently on lisinopril; formal diagnosis of hypertension not clearly documented).
- Overweight per patient report.

Medications:
- Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Aspirin used occasionally — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol (acetaminophen) recommended for fever — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Amoxicillin — delayed prescription; start if no improvement in 24–48 hours; 1 tablet three times daily; dose/strength not documented.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Lives with wife; children have moved out.
- Employment: Factory worker (manufactures steel parts).
- Tobacco: Occasional cigarette use; actively cutting down; using a vaporizer.
- Alcohol: Approximately 9 pints of beer per week (about 4 pints on Saturday and some on Sunday).

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (telephone consultation).
- Clinician noted audible nasal congestion (“sniffles”) on call.

Investigations:
- None discussed or performed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute viral upper respiratory infection vs early influenza; mild dyspnea reported; no chest pain.
  - Plan:
    - Rest and maintain hydration.
    - Paracetamol (acetaminophen) for fever/sweats (dose not documented).
    - Delayed antibiotic strategy: amoxicillin 1 tablet three times daily (dose/strength not documented) to start only if not improving after 24–48 hours or if persistent breathlessness/run-down.
    - Follow-up: If not better by next week, return for reassessment.
- Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  - Plan:
    - Continue metformin as currently prescribed (dose not documented). No changes discussed.
- Issue 3: History of high blood pressure.
  - Plan:
    - Continue lisinopril as currently prescribed (dose not documented). No changes discussed.
- Issue 4: Tobacco use (cutting down; using vaporizer).
  - Plan:
    - Encouraged smoking cessation.

General Plan items:
- None additional documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing/expected elements:
  - Vitals (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation) not obtained.
  - No physical exam beyond audible congestion; no objective respiratory assessment.
  - Medication doses, routes, and frequencies largely not documented.
  - No testing (e.g., COVID/influenza) discussed; vaccination status not discussed.
  - No explicit safety-net/red flag advice documented beyond follow-up if not better.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Dyspnea: patient initially suggests no increased breathlessness, later states breathing “not good” and confirms shortness of breath (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversational with fillers/overlaps; some unclear segments; clinically relevant details generally obtainable.
